content.introduction: According to Bloomberg Senior Editor for Technology and Strategic Industries Mike Shepard, disappointing Big Tech earnings are intensifying investor concerns about whether massive AI spending will generate sufficient returns, particularly affecting Alphabet and Intel. Shepard discusses these concerns on Bloomberg This Weekend, alongside hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo. The discussion highlights the struggles of companies like Intel due to inadequate memory supply and the challenges faced by traditional core areas of Alphabet and Amazon in sectors like ecommerce and advertising. Despite these concerns, the big hyperscalers, including Meta, Google, and Amazon, continue to push ahead with their AI investment plans.

Posted: 2026-10-31
Bloomberg Senior Editor for Technology and Strategic Industries Mike Shepard tells Bloomberg This Weekend that disappointing Big Tech earnings are intensifying investor concerns about whether massive AI spending will generate sufficient returns, as Alphabet and Intel come under particular pressure. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Shepard also discusses the record $6.3 billion Binance hack and the possibility that North Korean hackers were responsible. [4:28] that adequate supply of memory, companies like Intel are really struggling, but they're feeling it especially
[4:34] because they are in the midst of this turnaround under the new CEO, Lip Bu Tan, and this is yet another hurdle. He said he was more than a bit disappointed with [...] [1:24] return. And the question then became, well, what about the big hyperscalers, the cloud providers like
[1:30] Meta, Google, and Amazon? What will their results tell us? And the tale that take from the past week and a half really has been that they are pushing ahead with all
[1:39] those plans for AI investment, but the underlying business, especially some of the traditional core areas
[1:45] like for Alphabet and like for Amazon in areas like ecommerce and advertising, that's showing more
